correctness.rationale: For m>=2 each private clique plus its core vertex has exactly one positive vertex, necessarily label 2. Independence of chosen core-2 vertices yields m^{n-|S|} bijective choices and constant weight 2n. At m=1 core-1 is forbidden; independent core-2 set S and leaf choices exactly on N_H(S) give the second polynomial. For C_n, cycle gap analysis proves min weight and all optimum counts, and the 3x3 transfer weights each indexed cyclic bit word exactly once. All 13 brute-force instance distributions matched and matrix identities were checked.

value.rationale: The m=1 versus m>=2 boundary is structurally meaningful: increasing private clique size from one to two removes all nonconstant weight spectra. The arbitrary-base formula identifies the exact connection with the independence polynomial and with open neighborhoods, and the sunlet specialization determines every coefficient and a nontrivial three-residue optimizer multiplicity. These are natural configuration counts not obtainable from a scalar minimum, and distinguish two graph-operation regimes.
